# N13. lmh-patch: Megatron's LM-head forward and dgrad routed to K16, the dgrad through a sha-checked copy of Megatron's backward

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Switch: `AK_LMH=1` (config L40; owned by K16) · In the submitted runs: **on** · Class: **E0** · Rule basis: Graph Execution (TR-8.3)

**L4 v3.** This item is L4 v2's, byte for byte, in L4 v3's image: the same module (`2b32b7ce`), with K16's extension
(`ac552487`) and pin (`60104c48`). Tests that ran on L4 v2's image (package `firmus_gb300_ngpu8_llama8b_l4_nvfp4_v2`, withdrawn from this submission; see [Index](../KERNELS.md))
are labelled so in Evidence.

## In brief

NVIDIA's recipe computes the LM head (the output layer that maps the final hidden state to the 128,256 vocabulary
logits) in Megatron's code: the forward as `torch.matmul(x, W.t())` in the function `_linear_forward`, and the gradient
with respect to the layer's input (the dgrad) as the line `grad_input = grad_output.matmul(weight)` of the backward
`LinearWithGradAccumulationAndAsyncCommunication.backward`. N13, a Python patch module, sends both products to K16's
GEMMs on pinned cuBLASLt algorithms ([K16_lmh_lm_head.md](K16_lmh_lm_head.md)): it wraps `_linear_forward`, and it
replaces the backward with a copy compiled from Megatron's own source text with only the dgrad line changed, built only
when that text's sha256 is the one recorded in K16's pin file. N13 adds no arithmetic, so every output byte comes from
K16 (byte-identical to torch's matmul, K16's argument) or from Megatron's unchanged code.
**Result:** on this image, through the installed hooks, both GEMMs equal torch's matmul at their first call in the smoke
and all ten runs, and K16's kit, which patches Megatron with its own development copy of this module, found the LM-head
call byte-equal to stock; the eager-mode comparison in training ran on L4 v2's image.

## What it replaces (Replaces)

In Megatron's `megatron/core/tensor_parallel/layers.py`:

- **`_linear_forward`**, the module-level function that the forwards of Megatron's linear autograd Functions call for
  the GEMM. With no bias and no output dtype distinct from the input's, it returns `torch.matmul(input, weight.t())`.
  N13 replaces the module attribute with a wrapper. Callers in that module look the name up when they run, so they
  reach the wrapper: the forward of `LinearWithGradAccumulationAndAsyncCommunication` (the LM head's) and the forward of
  `LinearWithFrozenWeight`.
- **`LinearWithGradAccumulationAndAsyncCommunication.backward`**, the backward of the autograd Function that
  `linear_with_grad_accumulation_and_async_allreduce` (the LM head's call) applies. N13 replaces it with a copy in which
  only the dgrad line `grad_input = grad_output.matmul(weight)` is changed, to
  `grad_input = _ak_lmh_dgrad(grad_output, weight)`.
- **Unchanged:** every other line of that backward: the weight gradient (Megatron's APEX `wgrad_gemm_accum_fp16` call,
  which accumulates onto `main_grad`, Megatron's per-parameter gradient buffer), the `grad_added_to_main_grad` flag
  (Megatron's per-parameter mark that the gradient is already in `main_grad`), the tensor-parallel communication
  branches and the returned gradients.
- Lines in Megatron-LM `f6c33bde`, the commit the image installs, read on dev image 0929's copy of that commit:
  `_linear_forward` L516-540 (the branch N13 takes: L523-527); its two callers L492 and L698; the backward L700-875,
  with its dgrad line at L748; `linear_with_grad_accumulation_and_async_allreduce` L878-991.
- The two GEMMs, and what computes them instead, are K16's. N13 is the wiring.

## Where the code is (Source)

- **Patch module:** `firmus/ak/pkg/ak_l8b_lmh_patch.py`, sha256 `2b32b7ce`. Pure Python. It loads K16's extension

- **Installed** by section 5 of the image build (F5): Dockerfile L157-159 runs `pip install` on `firmus/ak/pkg`, whose

  site-packages as `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/ak_l8b_lmh_patch.py`. The package `firmus_ak` imports it
  (`firmus/ak/pkg/firmus_ak/__init__.py` L18). The build then runs `check_install.py` (Dockerfile L159).
- **Recorded, not re-hashed at run time.** The image's source record `/FIRMUS_AK_SOURCE_SHA256.txt` (written at
  Dockerfile L178) lists the source copy at `2b32b7ce` (record R9). The integrity banner at `import firmus_ak`
  re-hashes the build record (22 files under `/opt/firmus/ak`, K16's `.so` and pin among them) and the stack record
  (the 10 patched upstream and recipe files) (`firmus/ak/pkg/firmus_ak/banner.py` L26-27, L68, L83), not this module:
  its installed bytes are bound by the image's sha256 and the source record
  ([enablement and fail-loud behaviour](../KERNELS.md#enablement-and-fail-loud-behaviour)). Before the kits ran, the kit
  runner's image check found each of the 8 installed patch modules, this one included, equal to its packaged copy
  (record R5).
- **Against the development version.** `firmus/ak/pkg/diffs/ak_l8b_lmh_patch.diff` is the unified diff from the
  validated development version (sha256 `69d551d9`). `firmus/ak/pkg/CHANGES_vs_validated.md` (L32, L64-78) lists its 9
  edits: it arms on `AK_LMH` alone (no program-name (`sys.argv`) test, no `AK_LMH_FORCE` override); its kernel directory
  defaults to `/opt/firmus/ak/lmh` (it was the module's own `ext/` sibling); it fails loud (a pinned problem first met
  inside CUDA-graph capture raises, where it ran stock; a pinned algorithm missing from cuBLASLt's list raises, where it
  printed "NOT ARMED" and ran stock; a failed dgrad install raises at import, where it kept the stock dgrad); its
  docstring is updated. The forward wrapper and the lines that build the dgrad copy lie outside the diff's hunks: they
  are unchanged.

## Why the result is the same (Equivalence)

**NVIDIA's code** (Megatron-LM `f6c33bde`):

```
forward   LinearWithGradAccumulationAndAsyncCommunication.forward:
              return _linear_forward(total_input, weight, bias, output_dtype)
          _linear_forward, bias None, output_dtype None or the input's:
              return torch.matmul(input, weight.t())
backward  LinearWithGradAccumulationAndAsyncCommunication.backward   (decorated @staticmethod, @custom_bwd)
              ...
              grad_input = grad_output.matmul(weight)                # the dgrad line
              ...                                                    # wgrad onto main_grad, flags, TP branches, return
```

**N13:**

```
forward   layers._linear_forward = wrapper
          wrapper(input, weight, bias, output_dtype):
              if bias is None and output_dtype in (None, input.dtype):
                  out = _lm_forward(input, weight)                   # K16's GEMM, or None if the call is not K16's case
                  if out is not None: return out
              return original_linear_forward(input, weight, bias, output_dtype)
backward  src = source text of the unwrapped stock backward
          require sha256(src) == lmh_pin.json "bwd_src_sha256" and src has the dgrad line exactly once, else raise
          body = src without its decorator lines, dedented, with the dgrad line changed to
                     grad_input = _ak_lmh_dgrad(grad_output, weight)
          compile body; execute it with the layers module's own namespace as its globals
          layers._ak_lmh_dgrad = _lm_dgrad
          LinearWithGradAccumulationAndAsyncCommunication.backward = staticmethod(custom_bwd(copy))
          _lm_dgrad(g, w) = K16's GEMM if the call is K16's case, else g.matmul(w)
```

**The argument.**
- **The wrapper takes only the branch that is a plain matmul.** With no bias and the default output dtype, Megatron's
  function returns `torch.matmul(input, weight.t())` and does nothing else. The wrapper returns K16's output for exactly
  that product (byte-identical, K16). In every other case it calls the original function, including every call that
  K16's problem test or pin declines.
- **The copied backward is Megatron's text.** The source text must hash to the sha256 recorded when the pin was made, so
  the copy is made from one known text, and only the dgrad line changes. The other lines are compiled unchanged and run
  with Megatron's own module namespace as their globals, so every name they use (the APEX wgrad call, the memory buffer,
  the communication functions, the TE helpers) resolves to the same object as in the stock function. The only decorator
  lines in that text are `@staticmethod` and `@custom_bwd` (torch's mixed-precision decorator for a custom backward, as
  Megatron's module binds it). The copy strips them and re-applies the module's `custom_bwd` and `staticmethod`, in the
  same order.
- **The new dgrad call is the old line or K16.** `_lm_dgrad` returns K16's output for the LM head's case (byte-identical
  to `grad_output.matmul(weight)`, K16) and runs `grad_output.matmul(weight)` itself otherwise. Other users of this
  backward are unchanged.
- **The recorded text.** In Megatron-LM `f6c33bde` (dev image 0929's copy, clean against that commit) the backward's
  text, `layers.py` L700-875, hashes to `a939788f`, the pin's `bwd_src_sha256`. It has one dgrad line (L748) and no
  decorator lines other than L700-701. This was computed from the file's text for this write-up (record R10).
  On this image the install guard (Gate) accepted the image's backward text in the smoke and in every scored run, each
  of which installed the copy (Evidence). The pin check on L4 v2's image, with the same pin file (`60104c48`), printed
  the same source sha256 and dgrad count (record R12).

**Class E0**, as K16: byte-identical to the stock path on every tested input.

**State kept between calls:** no values: the wrapper at `layers._linear_forward` (the original kept as its
`__wrapped__`), the name `_ak_lmh_dgrad` in that module, the class's copied `backward` and the flag `dgrad_installed`,
all set once when Megatron's `layers` module is imported and never changed (read from `ak_l8b_lmh_patch.py` L191-205,
L208-227, L230-254); the per-problem state of the two entry points is K16's (K16, Equivalence).

## Numerics (Numerics)

N13 does no arithmetic. The wrapper hands the inputs to K16 or to Megatron's function, and the copied backward is
Megatron's text with one call changed. The numerics are K16's: bf16 in and out, fp32 accumulation, one rounding to bf16
(K16, Numerics).

## Optimizer and gradient clipping (Optimizer, Gradient clipping)

- Optimizer: Not applicable: N13 changes how the LM head's forward and input gradient are reached; it does not touch
  weights or optimizer state.
- Gradient clipping: Not applicable: the weight gradient that clipping reads comes from the copied backward's unchanged
  lines (the APEX wgrad onto `main_grad`), as in Megatron's code.

## Inputs it accepts (Shape specialisation)

### Gate

- **The forward wrapper** takes K16's path only when there is no bias and the output dtype is unset or the input's
  (`ak_l8b_lmh_patch.py` L194-198). K16's problem test and pin then decide (W exactly [128256, 4096] bf16 and
  contiguous, the pinned T = 16,384 rows; K16, Gate). Every other call runs Megatron's `_linear_forward`.
- **The copied backward** sends every call to `_lm_dgrad`, which takes K16 only for K16's case and otherwise runs the
  stock line (L175-188).
- **Install-time guard on the replaced code.** The unwrapped stock backward's source must hash to `lmh_pin.json`'s
  `bwd_src_sha256` (`a939788f`) and contain the dgrad line exactly once; otherwise the import of Megatron's `layers`
  module raises (L208-217). The count is over that one function: in `f6c33bde` another backward
  (`LinearWithFrozenWeight.backward`, L507) has the same line text, and N13 does not touch it.
- **Raises, no fallback:** the install guard above; any other failure of the install, which is not caught (L205); K16's
  raises at the first call of a problem (the pinned descriptor not in cuBLASLt's list, a first call inside CUDA-graph
  capture, a cuBLASLt error; K16, Gate).
- **`AK_LMH_DGRAD=0`**, a value the leaf does not set (the code default is 1), would keep the dgrad stock: no copy is
  made, and the run-start gate has no "lmh dgrad" row (`ak_l8b_lmh_patch.py` L39, L203-204;
  `firmus/ak/pkg/firmus_ak/run_start_gate.py` L67).
- The recipe's calls (x [8192, 2, 4096], dy [8192, 2, 128256]) are described in K16 (Gate).

### Assumptions not checked in code

1. **Megatron's `_linear_forward`, on the branch the wrapper takes, is `torch.matmul(input, weight.t())`.** N13 checks
   the sha256 of the backward it copies, but not the source of the forward function it wraps, and the forward's
   first-call check compares K16 with `torch.matmul(x, W.t())`, not with the wrapped function. What keeps it true: in
   the image's Megatron (`f6c33bde`, L523-527) that is what the branch computes, and the image's sha256 binds Megatron's
   files; on L4 v2's image an eager-mode comparison in training found the installed wrapper's output equal to Megatron's own function on every compared call (0 of 82 differed on each of the 8 ranks; Evidence).
   If it failed (a Megatron whose branch did something else), the LM head would keep computing the plain product and
   no check in the package would notice: **SILENT**.
2. **K16's assumption that later calls compute as the first.** The checks run on the first call of each problem only;
   every later call, including every captured timed step and every evaluation, runs unchecked: **SILENT** (K16,
   Assumptions not checked in code).

The other preconditions raise (Gate).

### Benchmark detection

N13 selects the code it replaces by name (Megatron's `_linear_forward` and the backward of
`LinearWithGradAccumulationAndAsyncCommunication`), and it builds the dgrad copy only from a backward source with a
recorded sha256. That is the identity of the replaced code, a property of the software stack, not of the benchmark (the
index's guards on the identity of the replaced code). Which calls take K16 is decided by K16's shape test (the LM head's
weight shape and the pinned row count; K16, Benchmark detection). The shipped module has no program-name test; the
development version had one (Source). N13 does not change results by detecting the benchmark (Benchmark detection is
not allowed, TR-2.3).

## How it is switched on and checked at run time (Enablement)

- **Switch:** K16's `AK_LMH=1` (config L40). N13 has no switch of its own; the leaf's
  comment on the line above the switch names both items ("K16, N13"). `AK_LMH` is read once, when the module is imported
  (`ak_l8b_lmh_patch.py` L38); the default is `"0"`, off. `AK_LMH_DGRAD` (L39; code default `"1"`, read only when
  armed) and `AK_LMH_DIR` (L40; default `/opt/firmus/ak/lmh`, which the image's `ENV` also sets, Dockerfile L139)
  are not in the leaf.
- **Import order.** `pretrain.py`'s first import is `firmus_ak`. Its `__init__.py` runs the integrity banner first (L13)
  and then imports this module, fourth of the eight patch modules (L18), before torch, TE or Megatron are imported.
  - Armed, the module installs an import hook for `megatron.core.tensor_parallel.layers` (L230-250, L253-254). If
    Megatron's module is already loaded, it patches it at once (L247-248).
  - When Megatron's module is first imported, the hook runs `_patch_layers` (L191-205): the wrapper, then, with the
    dgrad on, `_install_dgrad` (L208-227). A failure there raises at that import, at process start
    (`firmus/ak/pkg/CHANGES_vs_validated.md` L73-77).
- **First-call checks:** K16's, made inside these hooks on the first eager call of each problem, in NVIDIA's untimed
  warm-up (K16, Enablement). They compare each GEMM's output with torch's matmul; they do not compare the copied
  backward's other outputs. Every rank runs its own checks; rank 0 prints the two ARMED lines (the lines printed when a
  replacement arms, with its first-call verdict). Both lines name K16's extension and its sha; no line prints this
  module's sha.
  - The dgrad line is printed by `_lm_dgrad`, which only the copied backward calls (`ak_l8b_lmh_patch.py` L221), so it
    shows that the copy was installed and ran. The forward line is printed through `_lm_forward`, which only the
    wrapper calls (L196).
- **Run-start gate** (Firmus's check at the end of NVIDIA's warm-up that every armed part ran its first-call check):
  rows "lmh forward" (the forward problem checked) and "lmh dgrad" (the copy installed and the dgrad problem checked)
  (`firmus/ak/pkg/firmus_ak/run_start_gate.py` L63-69). A rank with an unchecked row raises before `run_start`
  (L120-131). The verdict is per rank, not all-reduced
  ([enablement and fail-loud behaviour](../KERNELS.md#enablement-and-fail-loud-behaviour)).

## Approval (Approval)

None needed. N13 is E0 and adds no arithmetic: it routes the LM head's two bf16 GEMMs to K16, which keeps their formats
and bytes. Graph Execution (TR-8.3) allows mathematically equivalent changes to the non-weight parts of the computation.

## Evidence (Evidence)

**Result on the submitted image:** PASS: on this image, through the installed hooks, both GEMMs equal torch's matmul at
their first call in the smoke run and all ten scored runs, and K16's kit found the LM-head call, patched by the kit's
development copy of this module, byte-equal to stock; on L4 v2's image, with the same module, an eager-mode comparison
in training found the installed hooks' outputs equal to Megatron's own code on every compared call.

The kit below is one of the 24 re-targeted kits run on this image's installed files, 48 / 48 PASS (R5).

- **Image checks** (R13): importing `firmus_ak` in the clean image prints the banner `MATCH` and imports all eight patch
  modules, `ak_l8b_lmh_patch` among them; the kit runner's image check is in Source. The build's install, import and
  banner tests: [the index](../KERNELS.md#tests-before-the-scored-runs).
- **K16's kit, PASS in both forms** (R5): as written, and with the allocator cache first filled with random bytes. The
  kit (K16's frozen development tests, re-targeted at the image) checks the image's `ak_l8b_lmh.so` (`ac552487`) and
  `lmh_pin.json` (`60104c48`) by sha (kit log L8-9). Its patch test imports the kit's own development copy of N13's
  module (`firmus/ak/csrc/lmh/test_lmh.py` L289-290), not the image's `ak_l8b_lmh_patch.py`, so it compares stock
  Megatron with Megatron patched by that copy, whose hook code is the shipped module's (Source). With FAILURES 0 (L52):
  - Megatron's `linear_with_grad_accumulation_and_async_allreduce` at the LM head's shapes (x [8192, 2, 4096],
    W [128256, 4096] with a bf16 `main_grad`, gradient-accumulation fusion on), first stock, then patched, on two seeds:
    output, input gradient and `main_grad` byte-equal (L47-48);
  - the patch reports "armed True, dgrad installed True" and the backward replaced (L44), so its source check accepted
    the image's backward text; two calls of each GEMM (L49);
  - a negative control: one flipped output bit in a fresh first call raises and leaves the problem unchecked (L51).
- **2 × 4 smoke run** (R13): 800 steps of the submitted config on this image. The forward and dgrad lines (smoke log
  L889, L891) are `True`; the run-start gate line (L946) lists "lmh forward" and "lmh dgrad" among its 19 armed parts
  and ends `True`, before `run_start` (L950); all 56 proof lines are present.

### Tests on L4 v2's image

L4 v2's submitted image; its files differ from L4 v3's only in N11's module, the run-start gate, the leaf's one added
switch, four comments or docstrings, and the three rebuilt extensions (K10, K11, K12). N13's module (`2b32b7ce`) and
K16's extension and pin are the same files in both.

- **Unit test of the installed module, PASS** (R1, R2): it arms the image's own modules through `import firmus_ak`, as
  `pretrain.py` does, with the L4 v2 leaf's switches and no file mounted over them, checks that N13's module is armed
  and loaded the image's extension (by the module's own record of the `.so` sha), then calls the module's two entry
  points, `_lm_forward(x, W)` and `_lm_dgrad(dy, W)`, directly, against `torch.matmul(x, W.t())` and `dy.matmul(W)`, on
  visible, reseeded, hidden, shape-variant and edge cases (K16, Evidence, gives the cases). Every output was byte-equal,
  and again with inputs at other addresses and in an eager, capture and replay sequence. So it grades, in the image's
  own file, what the hooks call: K16's problem test, the pin lookup, a row count without a pin running stock, the
  first-call checks and K16's GEMMs. The installed module matched the package's copy (`2b32b7cec41dba73`).
- **In-training comparison, eager mode** (R4): an eager-mode training run of the L4 leaf at DP 8, every site compared
  every 64 steps (18 compared steps per rank). The tool wraps whatever function is installed at `layers._linear_forward`
  and `layers._ak_lmh_dgrad`, here N13's wrapper and the dgrad function its copied backward calls, and compares each
  call's output with Megatron's own `_linear_forward` (the function under N13's wrapper) and with
  `grad_output.matmul(weight)`: forward 0 of 82 calls differed, dgrad 0 of 18, on each of the 8 ranks. It compares the
  forward's output and the dgrad value, on calls made outside CUDA-graph capture.
- **Model-level comparison** (R6): DP-4 training loops on mock data, the bundle against the bundle with one item switched
  off; no arm switched the LM head alone off. The stock arm (every `AK_*` switch unset) gave all 200 losses and the
  evaluation at step 200 identical to the bundle's, on the one trajectory observed. In the 50-step loops the two bundle
  loops departed from each other at step 45, and the stock loop from a bundle loop at step 42
  ([run-to-run reproducibility](../KERNELS.md#run-to-run-reproducibility)).
- **The pin check** (`make_pin.py --check`, R12): among the pin's other entries it confirmed, on the image's Megatron,
  the stock backward's source sha256 `a939788f` with one dgrad line (K16, Evidence).

### Training

- N13 was armed in all ten submitted runs; both of K16's first-call lines, made through N13's hooks, are `True` in each.
  For convergence see the [index](../KERNELS.md).
- On dev image 0929 (NVIDIA's 2026-09-29 release image, with the kernel files mounted), with the development version of
  this module (`69d551d9`) and K16's development build, 300-step training loops alternating the development stack
  without and with the LM-head path gave bit-identical losses and evaluations, with both lmh lines `True` (R7).
